research_question: What is the effect of laparoscopic hysterectomy (LAVH, TLH, or unspecified LH), compared with vaginal hysterectomy, on the need for blood transfusion in women undergoing hysterectomy for benign gynaecological disease?
outcome_description: Number of women who received a blood transfusion (intra-operative or post-operative) out of the total number randomised to each arm (intention-to-treat denominator)
positive_direction: Fewer blood transfusions in laparoscopic hysterectomy compared to vaginal hysterectomy
search_queries: laparoscopic vaginal hysterectomy blood transfusion randomized trial
laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy vaginal hysterectomy controlled trial
total laparoscopic hysterectomy vaginal hysterectomy transfusion outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing any laparoscopic hysterectomy technique (TLH, LAVH, or unspecified LH) directly with vaginal hysterectomy in women undergoing surgery for benign gynaecological disease
Studies reporting quantitative data on the occurrence of blood transfusion (intra-operative or post-operative) by randomised group
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, comments, or conference abstracts lacking full data)
Non-randomised studies or studies without a direct comparison between laparoscopic hysterectomy and vaginal hysterectomy (including comparisons limited to abdominal or robotic hysterectomy)
Studies conducted exclusively in patients with gynaecological malignancies
No quantitative outcome data reported on blood transfusion events or arm sample sizes (denominators)
moderators_to_extract: Laparoscopic technique variant (TLH vs. LAVH vs. LH unspecified)
Mean uterine weight or uterine size inclusion threshold
Definition/timing of transfusion assessed (intra-operative, post-operative, or both)
effect_size_note: Odds ratio (OR) pooled using fixed-effect Mantel-Haenszel model (or random-effects model if unavailable). An OR > 1 indicates a higher odds of blood transfusion with laparoscopic hysterectomy; an OR < 1 indicates lower odds of blood transfusion with laparoscopic hysterectomy. Multi-arm trials with multiple laparoscopic arms share/split the vaginal hysterectomy sample size and events to prevent double-counting. Zero-event studies in both arms are recorded with arm sizes and retained.
